body.text: Paint or Stain: Which Is Right for Your Fence

Paint and stain solve different problems, and it is worth being clear on the difference before booking either. Stain, covered on our /fence-staining page, penetrates the wood and lets the grain show through, which most homeowners in Kitchener-Waterloo prefer for cedar and pressure-treated fences. Paint sits on top of the wood as a solid, opaque film, which is the right call when you want a specific colour that does not exist as a wood tone, when you are matching trim or siding, or when the fence has already been painted and stripping it back to bare wood is not practical. If you are not sure which fits your situation, we will walk through both during the quote.
Why Prep Work Decides How Long Paint Lasts

Most fence paint failures we get called to fix did not start as a paint problem, they started as a prep problem. Paint applied over dirt, mildew, or a peeling old coat has nothing solid to grip onto, so it lifts and flakes within a season or two, often faster on fences that face direct afternoon sun. We start every paint job with a full clean to strip away grime and any failing paint, followed by repairs to loose boards or popped fasteners, and finish with a primer coat before any colour goes on. It is more work upfront, but it is the reason our painted fences hold their finish for years instead of needing touch-ups by the following summer.

body.text: Paint That Handles Southwestern Ontario Weather

We use durable exterior paints designed to handle the swings this region throws at outdoor wood, from humid summer afternoons to freezing winter nights. A quality exterior paint applied over properly primed wood resists cracking through those temperature swings far better than a bargain product applied over bare or dirty wood, regardless of how many coats go on. We also use environmentally friendly formulations that are safe for kids, pets and garden beds along the fence line, since most of the yards we work in are in active use the same week we finish.

One advantage paint has over stain is colour flexibility. Where stain tones are limited to variations on natural wood colours, paint opens up the full range, from classic white and grey picket fences to darker charcoal tones that have become popular on newer builds across Kitchener and Waterloo. We can help match an existing colour on your property, such as trim, siding or a garage door, or start fresh with something new.
Painting New Wood vs Repainting an Older Fence

New pressure-treated fencing generally needs time to dry out before it will hold paint, often a full season depending on how it was milled and stored before installation, so painting a brand-new fence right away is one of the more common mistakes we see. Older fences carry the opposite challenge: previous coats of paint, sun damage and weathering all need to be addressed during prep rather than painted over. We treat these as two different jobs with two different timelines rather than applying the same approach to both, which is part of why our repaints hold up longer than a quick weekend job.

A properly primed and painted fence in this region typically holds its finish for three to five years before it needs attention again, with south- and west-facing sections often showing wear first due to greater sun exposure. Chalking, fading or the first signs of peeling at joints and end grain are the usual indicators that it is time to book another coat.

If your fence has flaking paint from a previous job, do not paint over it. We strip failing paint back during the cleaning stage so the new coat has a stable surface, rather than layering fresh paint on top of a coat that is already lifting.

faqs.q: How often should I repaint my fence?
faqs.a: Most painted fences in Kitchener-Waterloo need a fresh coat every three to five years, depending on sun exposure and the quality of the previous paint job.

faqs.q: Can you paint over an old colour?
faqs.a: Yes. We clean and prime over the existing colour first, and may recommend fully stripping any areas where the old paint is already peeling before applying the new coat.

faqs.q: How long does fence painting take?
faqs.a: Timing depends on the fence's size and condition, but most projects run about two to three days including cleaning, repairs, priming and two coats of paint.

faqs.q: Will the paint be safe for my kids, pets and garden?
faqs.a: Yes, we use environmentally friendly paints and cleaning products that are safe once dry for pets, plants and family use of the yard.

faqs.q: Should I choose paint or stain for my fence?
faqs.a: Paint gives full, opaque colour and the widest colour range, while stain shows off the wood grain and is generally lower maintenance to renew. We can help you decide based on your fence's condition and the look you want.
